Don't miss — $1-3 gems, good buys and $4-10 value

Gems and Good: camp check of 10 Oct (reasons on the $1-3 buys tab and in the instant call). Value: usually $4-10 and worth $6+ more. Bid up to the cap; "usual" is what the room paid in the simulated drafts.

Must-get ladder — what actually moves the roto

From 2,000 simulated drafts of this card: you land ~3 of the 13 primaries, ~5 pivots and ~5 one-dollar fills. Three things decide the season: the anchor, the second-star seat, and how many cheap value hits the room lets you have. The roto shown is projected 2026-27 roto on the 16-team scale: your simulated roster's season (with injury/variance noise) ranked against the 15 rival rosters drafted in the same simulated auction, at their projections — the same basis as the 2026-27 column on the scorecard. It assumes the projections are right and the rivals draft off Yahoo; against the real past standings with no streaming uplift the same drafts average 76.7. Let the cheap targets come up mid-draft rather than nominating them yourself: an early nomination only calls the sleeper hunters to the table.

Young players most likely to jump

Best $1-3 buys

Every player you get for $3 or less in at least half of 2,000 simulated drafts of this room. A draft where nobody bought him counts as a $1 buy: he was still there at the end. Ranked by Blend $, the value your caps use; Punt $ is our engine alone and "If repeat 25-26" is what his real 2025-26 season is worth on the same scale. Above top-150 average in lists the categories where his projection beats the average of the 150 most valuable players; a category in bold is one your team is behind in right now. Players sold or kept drop off as you log picks; yours turn green. Projected 20+ games only, no SKIP, no keepers.

Camp check (). Every player here was checked by hand against the training-camp news: his roster spot, injuries, who starts in preseason, and the age and health of the teammates ahead of him. Gem = clear value and a safe or growing role. Good = worth $1-3. Filler = fine for $1 to fill a slot. Risk = something in the news, or our engine alone, says be careful. These are judgements from the news, not model output, and they do not change Blend $ or Cap. Our minutes already give bench players a share of the games their starters usually miss; a Gem note means the news adds to that.

Young players who can grow into a role

If role grows is a what-if on the Punt $ scale: his own per-minute stats at the minutes and games shown, not a forecast that he gets them. Most of these are worth $0 at our projection and cost $1 or nothing, so the risk of a late $1 bid is small.

How to read this table

The full league, not just the draft board. Sort by any column. Every stat column from Age to FT% is our 2026-27 projection, per game — not last season. Last season appears only as the two rank columns, '25-26 tot' and '25-26 pg'. Yahoo $ is your league's pre-draft value, Punt $ is our engine's value with turnovers ignored, Blend $ is Punt $ averaged with Yahoo's own value on the same ladder — the value your Cap and Edge use, because the two together rank real seasons better than either alone — Pay ~ is what the room is expected to pay, Cap is your walk-away. Edge = Blend $ minus what he will actually cost you, which is max(top of Pay ~, Cap) — the same cost rule the bench, the chips and the roster optimiser use. ALMOC 24 / ALMOC 25 are what this room actually paid for him in the last two auctions — hover for the manager. Green edge = the room underprices him.

Best next buys

?How this works

Updated after every pick. The page builds the best 13-man plan your money still buys: it starts from the kit's Scenarios and your card, then searches thousands of one- and two-player swaps, scoring expected roto in all 9 categories against the simulated rivals.

Prices follow the room: if sales run hot or cold, the plan's prices move with them. The top 6 are the plan's biggest buys right now. "Worth +1.3 roto" means your final team scores 1.3 roto points more with him than without him, both sides re-planned in full; it is the same Roto +/- the Players table, his call and the what-if show. "Replaceable" means under 0.5, which is inside the search's noise. "If you miss him" lists the best one-for-one swaps. Everywhere on the page, a + next to a player means he helps your team.

Your turn to nominate?

Expensive players the room usually pays more for than your cap (call says ONLY IF CHEAP). Putting one up makes your rivals spend money before your targets come up. Do not put up your own gems: an early nomination calls the bargain hunters to the table. A common auction tactic, not something the simulator tested.

Live scenarios from what is left

Three $200 rosters built from the players still available, your own players included, at the price level you set. Generate after a pick to see your best plan and its roto points now. Cross a player off (✕) if you expect to lose him, and the three rosters rebuild. Roto = projected roto points against the simulated rivals.

Three rosters · and the elephant in the room

A player whose 2025-26 line looks good is not a sleeper. Across 365 ALMOC buys, the price this room pays is 81.2% explained by Yahoo $ plus last season's value plus the last one-to-two months. Everyone sees the same numbers, so anyone with a strong line or a hot finish gets bid up. Real hidden value has to be invisible in those columns: a role about to change, or per-minute production that never had minutes behind it. The Seen score below is how obvious each player already is — 0 means nobody is looking, 100 means everybody is. It now counts the summer's Rotoworld coverage, because every manager here reads it: a player the press has called a must-draft or a sleeper is not a sleeper. It also counts a rookie's draft slot and last year's Yahoo $, which is why the first overall pick and an injured star no longer show up as "hidden". Our own test also found the last one-to-two months does not predict next season once you know the season average. The room pays for it anyway. That gap is the edge.
Which number do I bid to? In a plan, its Max bid. The 13 Max bids of every plan add up to $200 or less, so a plan can never overspend. Cap is the hard walk-away when you are not following a plan (the caps of plan A add up to more than $200). A, B and C are the best $200 roster at three price levels of this room, from 2,000 simulated drafts: A if prices run low (each player at the room's 20th-percentile price), B at the usual price (median), C if you have to pay your full Cap. None contains a player the kit says SKIP, and nobody is priced above his Cap. Start the draft on B. If the first 20-30 picks go cheap, lean toward A; if they go expensive, lean toward C. You will not land all 13 of any list (the simulator lands about 3 of 13 main targets), so read each as who is worth chasing at that price level. All three score all nine categories, turnovers included, as the league does. D is the hidden-value list; its Max bid is your Cap.

What the simulator says

Words on this page

WordWhat it means
Yahoo $Yahoo's pre-draft value for your league (export of 10 Oct). The room starts from it.
Punt $What our engine says he is worth: his 2026-27 projection in 8 categories (turnovers ignored), on a 16-team $200 scale.
Blend $Our engine and Yahoo, half each. This is the "worth" that the caps, Edge and the Players sort use.
Pay ~What this room usually pays: the middle half of prices in 2,000 simulated drafts. Never below Yahoo $.
CapYour walk-away price. Never bid above it. How it is set is in the next table.
EdgeBlend $ minus the most he should cost you (the top of Pay ~ or your Cap, whichever is higher). Plus means a bargain.
Max bidMoney left minus $1 for every other open slot.
Repeat $What his real 2025-26 season would be worth on the same scale as Punt $.
Range $The 80% likely range of his season value.
Gem / Good / Filler / RiskThe camp check of the $1-3 players, read by hand from the news of 10 Oct.
ONLY IF CHEAPThe room usually pays more than he is worth to you. His cap is still shown: if the bidding stops under it, he is a buy. Your call.

Where the numbers come from

PartHowHow good
Stat linesOur engine: three seasons of per-minute stats with age curves, blended half-and-half with our growth model.Tested on 2020-21 to 2025-26: ranks real value better than the kit's old model (0.618 vs 0.601).
Minutes and gamesSeptember research on all 30 teams, updated with the news to 9 Oct. Bench players get the games their starters usually miss.Injury timelines follow one fixed rule. Nobody predicts games well.
Worth (Blend $)Our engine and Yahoo, half each.Ranked real seasons better than either alone: 0.679 vs 0.641 (engine) and 0.581 (Yahoo), 2020-21 to 2023-24.
Room prices (Pay ~)2,000 simulated drafts of this 16-team room; each manager bids like his own history.It uses our own projections, so it cannot tell us whether they are right.
$1-3 notesRead by hand from the training-camp news.Judgement, not a model.
Honest limitsOur engine alone still ranks players a little worse than the Yahoo market (0.573 vs about 0.60); that is why Blend $ mixes the two. It is too optimistic about young players improving: only about 41% of the jumps it projects really happen.
